paper.title: RoboPhD: Self-Improving Text-to-SQL Through Autonomous Agent Evolution
paper.central_claim: AI agents autonomously conduct research in a closed evolution loop (Evolution agent + ELO selection) that improves a Text-to-SQL agent package (Python database-analysis tool + SQL-generation instructions) from a trivial ~70-line baseline to 73.67% on the BIRD test set, with larger gains on cheaper executor models ('skip a tier').

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: not exposed to the worker by the configured model type; no extra probing per controller instruction.

sections_read: Appendix A-E (LLM usage, reproducibility, strategy prompt, selection protocol, naive baseline)

evidence.quote: RoboPhD evolves AI agents composed of two artifacts—a database analysis tool and SQL generation instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Defines the evolved object: a Python database-analysis tool plus a markdown instruction file (non-weight artifacts).

evidence.quote: Central to the framework is an ELO-based selection mechanism enabling survival-of-the-fittest dynamics while handling non-transitivity in performance.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated centrepiece: ELO selection over a population of agent packages.

evidence.quote: It receives ELO rankings, accuracy metrics, and detailed error analysis
evidence.support_explanation: Information visible to the Evolution AI when proposing a new package.

evidence.quote: The evolution process is guided by a hand-crafted strategy prompt; evolving these strategies themselves is future work
evidence.support_explanation: The improver (strategy prompt) is fixed and hand-written; no improver-level improvement.

evidence.quote: RoboPhD tests three agents selected via a priority system: (1) the previous winner, (2) the newly evolved agent, and (3) a random agent selected from the top 2 performers by ELO (other than the winner).
each iteration evaluates agents on only 5 randomly selected databases from the 69-database training set, with 30 randomly sampled questions per database
evidence.support_explanation: Fitness is measured on ~150 questions per iteration, resampled each iteration (selection set, noisy).

evidence.quote: While the evolved Opus agent improves by 2.3 points over naive Opus, the evolved Haiku agent gains 8.9 points
evidence.support_explanation: Dev-set gains (Table 1): Opus 69.0->71.3, Sonnet 65.7->69.2, Haiku 57.2->66.1 vs the naive package.

evidence.quote: Evolution improves overall accuracy by 1.51 points (73.67% vs 72.16%)
evidence.support_explanation: Official BIRD test result (Opus-4.5); Table 2 shows Simple -0.32, Moderate +1.80, Challenging +7.02.

evidence.quote: costs approximately $2 in Claude API for the calls and runs for 22 minutes on average
evidence.support_explanation: Per-iteration cost uses Haiku 4.5 as the SQL generator, i.e. evolution is run against the cheapest executor.

evidence.quote: each 30-iteration run uses about 12% of the weekly usage quota of a Claude Max plan
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution-agent (Claude Code) cost is expressed as quota share, not dollars/tokens.

evidence.quote: We experimented with alternative strategies (refinement, research-driven, error-focused) but found cross-pollination with tool-only emphasis consistently produced our strongest agents.
Our preliminary experiments show promise, but results remain ambiguous
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-evolution (improver-level) is explicitly not part of the evidence.

evidence.quote: You are an expert in the field of Text2SQL.
evidence.support_explanation: The hand-written strategy prompt invokes domain expertise of the Evolution LLM; 'no domain knowledge' means no author-supplied technique, not no LLM prior.

evidence.quote: There is some non-determinism that we cannot control in Claude Opus/Sonnet API responses that may lead to differences in the results when run from scratch.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge run-to-run variation of an evolutionary process; no repeated runs reported.

evidence.quote: —in the 18th round of evolution, the Evolution AI synthesized techniques from three parent agents that had each reached 76% training accuracy on the 17th iteration
evidence.support_explanation: The champion (iter18) was selected on training-database accuracy; the rule that picked it for dev/test submission is not stated.

evidence.quote: a large-scale cross-domain dataset with 69 training databases and 11 development databases
evidence.support_explanation: Evolution on train DBs; dev DBs are database-disjoint from training.

evidence.quote: Note that the AI models constructed by RoboPhD did not have independent access to private test data.
evidence.support_explanation: Test-set isolation statement; official test run by the BIRD team.

evidence.quote: Through competitive evaluation, tool-only execution emerged as superior for two reasons
evidence.support_explanation: Design choice (tool-only) justified by competitive evaluation inside the loop; numbers not shown.

evidence.support_explanation: Evolved artifacts are large (≈1000-line tool + 527-line instructions), so inference prompts and cost grow.

signatures.object: Agent package = tools/*.py database-analysis script + eval_instructions.md (naive baseline: 50-line DDL dump + 20-line instructions)
signatures.information: Evolution AI (Claude Code, Sonnet/Opus 4.5) sees ELO rankings, accuracy, error-analysis report and top agents' packages plus a hand-written cross-pollination strategy; the SQL model sees analysis output ⊕ instructions ⊕ question ⊕ BIRD evidence, never the schema directly; no test data.
signatures.operation: Evolution AI combines techniques of top agents and fixes error patterns into one new package; 'Deep Focus' re-tests the candidate against earlier iterations' questions in the same session and refines (k=1).
signatures.output: One new candidate package per iteration (plus reasoning.md).
signatures.conditions: Tool-only deterministic analysis required; 200K-token context limit forces size-adaptive analysis; Haiku-4.5 is the SQL generator during evolution.
signatures.feedback: Execution accuracy (BIRD set comparison) on 5 random train DBs x 30 questions per iteration.
signatures.selection_rule: Three-way competition (previous winner, new agent, random top-2 ELO), pairwise ELO update K=32; winner by raw accuracy; from iteration 12, 30% of iterations are non-evolution 'challenger/none' rounds.
signatures.persistence: All agent packages and ELO ratings are archived across iterations.
signatures.later_use: Winner and top-ELO agents are the parents shown to the next Evolution AI call; best package is deployed unchanged (analysis run once per DB offline).
signatures.failure_boundary: Single run; champion-selection rule, dev question count and per-iteration variance not reported; no ELO, Deep-Focus or artifact-level ablation.

gap.author_gap: Strong Text-to-SQL systems rely on manual prompt/architecture engineering and domain expertise; the paper wants agents to discover such strategies autonomously.
gap.checked_gap: The manual-engineering cost is a real, but generic, limitation. Related work covers Text-to-SQL systems and prompt optimisers (APE, OPRO, DSPy, TextGrad, ACE) and evolutionary NAS/HPO; code-level agent-evolution neighbours are not discussed in the material, and no head-to-head with any optimiser is given. The 'first ELO for evolutionary prompt/agent optimisation' claim was not checked (no external search).
lineage: prompt optimisers (APE/OPRO/DSPy/TextGrad/ACE) -> evolving complete agent artifacts (tool + instructions)
evolutionary NAS/HPO -> population with ELO rating
closest_adjacent: TextGrad (text-gradient analogy used by the authors)
BIRD leaderboard systems (CHASE-SQL, XiYan-SQL, AskData etc.; manual designs)
gap.residue: Whether LLM-driven evolution of executable analysis tools + instructions beats prompt-only optimisers or strong hand-engineered baselines is untested.
gap.stakes: Engineering effort per domain; cost-per-query tier choice.
gap.method_response: Co-evolve a deterministic analysis tool and instructions via cross-pollination under ELO selection.
gap.remaining_gap: No optimiser baselines, no meta-evolution result, single domain, single run.
unresolved: Nearest-neighbour agent-evolution papers not fixed locally; novelty of ELO selection unchecked.
Whether gains exceed a strong hand-written package of equal length.

M.reason: Mechanism is concretely reconstructable (artifacts, information, Deep Focus, ELO, size-adaptive discovery) and fits the problem; distinguishing predictions versus naive alternatives are not tested (between anchors 2 and 4).

E.measurement.reason: BIRD execution accuracy with official test by the BIRD team is a credible verifier; 150-question per-iteration fitness is noisy and the naive baseline is trivial (checked in E.causality, not here).

E.causality.reason: Only evolved-vs-naive on the same executor is shown. No ELO/selection, Deep-Focus, tool-vs-instruction, alternative-optimiser, or strong hand-written-baseline controls; strategy comparison asserted without data; inverse-scaling confounded by Haiku-based evolution.

E.holdout.reason: Evolution on 69 train DBs; dev DBs disjoint; official test held by BIRD; three executors. Unreported champion-selection rule, possible dev exposure during framework development and LLM pretraining contamination of BIRD keep it below 4.

E.statistics.reason: Single run, no seeds/intervals/significance despite author-acknowledged non-determinism and sub-point margins; dev denominator not stated; negative sub-result (Simple -0.32) is reported.

E.cost.reason: Per-iteration $2/22 min (Haiku side), per-query costs per tier, and quota share for 30 iterations are reported; Claude Code evolution cost not in tokens/$ and the 'lower cost' claim excludes it.
